title: find-non-sru-proposed script
description:
find-non-sru-proposed script

vibe coded script I used to help me to clear non-SRUs from stonking-proposed right after tenacious (devel) opened and the packages from stonking were copied over to tenacious.

The script is a bit on the large and perhaps complex side mostly because of all the retries I asked the agent to implement in case of flakiness.

It is not meant to be a source of truth: DO NOT run the removal commands blindly. It is a helper, and indeed it did help me to quickly remove dozens and dozens of packages from stonking-proposed, while only keeping a few around that I could then inspect manually without too much trouble.

+#!/usr/bin/python3
+

+# along with this program.  If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
+
+'''Find uploads in a stable release's -proposed that are not meant as SRUs.
+
+A source package in <release>-proposed is considered a non-SRU when:
+
+  * the exact same source version is published in <devel>-proposed, and
+  * the upload does not reference any Launchpad bug.
+
+Bug references are taken from the pending SRU report (sru_report.yaml).
+Because that report also lists no bugs when it could not determine them,
+an empty bug list is confirmed against the Launchpad-Bugs-Fixed field of
+the upload's .changes file.
+
+Nothing is removed: the matching remove-package commands are printed on
+stdout for review, one per package followed by a grouped command at the
+end.
+'''
+
+import argparse
+import datetime
+import email.utils
+import http.client
+import logging
+import os
+import shlex
+import signal
+import socket
+import sys
+import time
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+
+import httplib2
+import yaml
+from debian.changelog import Changelog
+from debian.debian_support import Version
+from launchpadlib.launchpad import Launchpad
+from lazr.restfulclient.errors import ServerError
+
+
+SRU_REPORT_URL = (
+    "https://static-reports.ubuntu.com/pending-sru/sru_report.yaml")
+DEFAULT_REASON = "Proposed cleanup, not meant for an SRU"
+# Overridden from the command line.
+RETRIES = 6
+TIMEOUT = 60
+# Upper bound in seconds for the exponential backoff between retries.
+MAX_BACKOFF = 60
+
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("find-non-sru-proposed")
+
+
+def describe(error):
+    '''Return a one-line description of error for log messages.
+
+    The str() of launchpadlib's HTTPError includes the full response
+    headers and body, so only its first line is kept.
+    '''
+    return "%s: %s" % (type(error).__name__, str(error).partition("\n")[0])
+
+
+# Errors from network access; is_transient() picks the ones worth retrying.
+NETWORK_ERRORS = (
+    urllib.error.URLError, http.client.HTTPException,
+    httplib2.HttpLib2Error, ServerError, ConnectionError, TimeoutError,
+    socket.timeout)
+
+
+def is_transient(error):
+    if isinstance(error, urllib.error.HTTPError):
+        return error.code >= 500 or error.code == 429
+    return isinstance(error, NETWORK_ERRORS)
+
+
+def retry(label, func, *args, **kwargs):
+    '''Call func(*args, **kwargs), retrying on transient network errors.
+
+    label identifies the operation in retry warnings.
+
+    Since launchpadlib fetches lazily, func should do all the network work
+    that has to be retried as a whole (e.g. iterating over a collection).
+    '''
+    for attempt in range(RETRIES + 1):
+        try:
+            return func(*args, **kwargs)
+        except Exception as e:
+            if not is_transient(e) or attempt == RETRIES:
+                raise
+            delay = min(2 ** attempt, MAX_BACKOFF)
+            logger.warning(
+                "%s: %s; retry %d/%d in %ds",
+                label, describe(e), attempt + 1, RETRIES, delay)
+            time.sleep(delay)
+
+
+def fetch_url(url):
+    def fetch():
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=TIMEOUT) as f:
+            return f.read()
+    return retry(url, fetch)
+
+
+def load_sru_report(location):
+    '''Load the SRU report YAML; return (data, modification time or None).
+
+    The modification time is the Last-Modified header for URLs and the
+    file mtime for local paths.
+    '''
+    if "://" in location:
+        def fetch():
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(location, timeout=TIMEOUT) as f:
+                return f.read(), f.headers.get("Last-Modified")
+        data, last_modified = retry(location, fetch)
+        mtime = None
+        if last_modified:
+            parsed = email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime(last_modified)
+            if parsed.tzinfo is None:
+                # HTTP dates are GMT; never read them as local time.
+                parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
+            mtime = parsed.timestamp()
+        return yaml.safe_load(data), mtime
+    with open(location) as f:
+        return yaml.safe_load(f), os.path.getmtime(location)
+
+
+def proposed_sources(archive, series):
+    '''Return {source name: {version: spph}} published in series-proposed.'''
+    def fetch():
+        sources = {}
+        for spph in archive.getPublishedSources(
+                distro_series=series, pocket="Proposed", status="Published"):
+            sources.setdefault(spph.source_package_name, {})[
+                spph.source_package_version] = spph
+        return sources
+    return retry("%s-proposed sources" % series.name, fetch)
+
+
+def baseline_version(archive, series, name):
+    '''Return the newest version of name in series outside -proposed.'''
+    def fetch():
+        return [
+            Version(spph.source_package_version)
+            for spph in archive.getPublishedSources(
+                source_name=name, exact_match=True, distro_series=series,
+                status="Published")
+            if spph.pocket != "Proposed"]
+    versions = retry("%s/%s publications" % (series.name, name), fetch)
+    return max(versions) if versions else None
+
+
+def changes_bugs(spph):
+    '''Return the bugs in Launchpad-Bugs-Fixed of spph's .changes file.
+
+    Return None if the upload has no .changes file (e.g. it was copied).
+    '''
+    url = retry("%s %s .changes URL" % (
+        spph.source_package_name, spph.source_package_version),
+        spph.changesFileUrl)
+    if url is None:
+        return None
+    for line in fetch_url(url).splitlines():
+        if line.startswith(b"Launchpad-Bugs-Fixed:"):
+            return [int(b) for b in line.split(b":", 1)[1].split()]
+    return []
+
+
+def changelog_bugs(spph, baseline):
+    '''Return the LP bugs closed in spph's changelog since baseline.
+
+    Without a baseline only the top entry is considered, as dpkg-genchanges
+    does by default.
+    '''
+    url = retry("%s %s changelog URL" % (
+        spph.source_package_name, spph.source_package_version),
+        spph.changelogUrl)
+    if url is None:
+        return None
+    changelog = Changelog(fetch_url(url).decode("utf-8", "replace"))
+    bugs = set()
+    for i, block in enumerate(changelog):
+        if baseline is None and i > 0:
+            break
+        if baseline is not None and block.version <= baseline:
+            break
+        bugs.update(block.lp_bugs_closed)
+    return sorted(bugs)
+
+
+def check_candidate(archive, release, name, version, spph, report_bugs,
+                    ignored_bugs):
+    '''Return whether name/version is removable, or None on network failure.
+
+    Removable means the upload does not reference any Launchpad bug, or
+    every bug it references is in ignored_bugs.
+    '''
+    report_version, bugs = report_bugs.get(name, (None, []))
+    if report_version == version and bugs:
+        bug_ids = [b["id"] for b in bugs]
+        if ignored_bugs and set(bug_ids) <= ignored_bugs:
+            logger.info(
+                "%s %s: SRU report lists only ignored bug(s) %s; "
+                "confirming against Launchpad",
+                name, version, " ".join(map(str, bug_ids)))
+        else:
+            logger.info(
+                "skipping %s %s: SRU report lists bugs %s",
+                name, version, " ".join(map(str, bug_ids)))
+            return False
+    # The SRU report also has an empty bug list when it could not determine
+    # the bugs, so check Launchpad.
+    try:
+        source = ".changes"
+        fixed = changes_bugs(spph)
+        if fixed is None:
+            source = "changelog"
+            fixed = changelog_bugs(spph, baseline_version(
+                archive, release, name))
+    except NETWORK_ERRORS as e:
+        # Skip the candidate on fetch failures (exhausted retries, or
+        # non-transient HTTP errors such as a missing .changes file); any
+        # other error is a bug in this script and propagates.
+        logger.warning(
+            "skipping %s %s: cannot determine bugs: %s",
+            name, version, describe(e))
+        return None
+    if fixed is None:
+        logger.warning("skipping %s %s: cannot determine bugs", name, version)
+        return False
+    if fixed:
+        if ignored_bugs and set(fixed) <= ignored_bugs:
+            logger.info(
+                "removing %s %s: %s closes only ignored bug(s) %s",
+                name, version, source, " ".join(map(str, fixed)))
+            return True
+        logger.info(
+            "skipping %s %s: %s closes bugs %s",
+            name, version, source, " ".join(map(str, fixed)))
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def print_commands(suite, reason, removals):
+    '''Print the remove-package commands for removals on stdout.
+
+    One command per (name, version) pinning the version with -e, then a
+    grouped command for all names: a shared command line cannot pin
+    versions, so that one removes the current version of each package.
+    '''
+    logger.info("%d removal candidate(s)", len(removals))
+    if not removals:
+        return
+    base_command = shlex.join(
+        ["remove-package", "-y", "-s", suite, "-m", reason])
+    print("# Individual removals (versions pinned with -e):")
+    for name, version in removals:
+        print(base_command, shlex.join([name, "-e", version]))
+    print()
+    print("# All candidates in one call (current versions):")
+    print(base_command, shlex.join(dict.fromkeys(
+        name for name, _ in removals)))
+    sys.stdout.flush()
+
+
+def parse_args():
+    '''Parse command line arguments.
+
+    Return (parser, args); the parser is returned too so that main() can
+    report errors found after querying Launchpad.
+    '''
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description=__doc__,
+        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-l", "--launchpad", dest="launchpad_instance", default="production")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-s", "--release",
+        help="stable release to clean up (default: current stable release)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-d", "--devel",
+        help="development release to compare against "
+             "(default: current development series)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--sru-report", default=SRU_REPORT_URL, metavar="URL_OR_PATH",
+        help="pending SRU report YAML (default: %(default)s)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--report-max-age", type=float, default=3.0, metavar="HOURS",
+        help="warn if the SRU report is older than HOURS "
+             "(0 disables the check; default: %(default)s)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-m", "--reason",
+        help="removal comment (default: %r)" % DEFAULT_REASON)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--ignore-bug", type=int, action="append", dest="ignored_bugs",
+        default=[], metavar="LP_BUG",
+        help="treat a candidate as bug-free if LP_BUG is the only bug "
+             "it fixes (may be given multiple times)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-v", "--verbose", action="store_true",
+        help="report progress while inspecting each candidate")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--limit", type=int, metavar="N",
+        help="check at most N candidates (default: no limit)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--retries", type=int, default=RETRIES,
+        help="retries on transient network errors (default: %(default)s)")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--timeout", type=int, default=TIMEOUT,
+        help="network timeout in seconds (default: %(default)s)")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.limit is not None and args.limit < 1:
+        parser.error("--limit must be at least 1")
+    if args.report_max_age < 0:
+        parser.error("--report-max-age must not be negative")
+    return parser, args
+
+
+def main():
+    global RETRIES, TIMEOUT
+    parser, args = parse_args()
+    logging.basicConfig(format="%(levelname).1s: %(message)s")
+    # Only this script's logger, so that libraries do not get chatty with -v.
+    logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG if args.verbose else logging.INFO)
+    # Treat termination like Ctrl-C, so that partial results get printed.
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.default_int_handler)
+
+    RETRIES = args.retries
+    TIMEOUT = args.timeout
+    # launchpadlib does not set a timeout on its own HTTP connections.
+    socket.setdefaulttimeout(TIMEOUT)
+
+    lp = Launchpad.login_anonymously(
+        "find-non-sru-proposed", args.launchpad_instance,
+        version="devel", timeout=TIMEOUT)
+
+    ubuntu = lp.distributions["ubuntu"]
+    archive = ubuntu.main_archive
+    if args.devel:
+        devel = ubuntu.getSeries(name_or_version=args.devel)
+    else:
+        devel = ubuntu.current_series
+    if args.release:
+        release = ubuntu.getSeries(name_or_version=args.release)
+    else:
+        stable = [s for s in ubuntu.series
+                  if s.status == "Current Stable Release"]
+        release = stable[0] if len(stable) == 1 else None
+    if release is None:
+        parser.error("cannot determine current stable release; use -s")
+    if release.name == devel.name:
+        parser.error("release and devel series must differ")
+    reason = args.reason or DEFAULT_REASON
+    logger.info(
+        "looking for non-SRUs in %s-proposed (devel: %s)",
+        release.name, devel.name)
+
+    logger.debug("fetching SRU report from %s", args.sru_report)
+    report, report_mtime = load_sru_report(args.sru_report)
+    report = report or {}
+    if report_mtime is None:
+        logger.warning("cannot determine the age of the SRU report")
+    elif args.report_max_age:
+        age = time.time() - report_mtime
+        if age > args.report_max_age * 3600:
+            logger.warning(
+                "SRU report is %.1f hours old (max: %s); "
+                "its bug data may be stale", age / 3600, args.report_max_age)
+    if release.name not in report:
+        logger.warning(
+            "%s not in SRU report; using Launchpad data only", release.name)
+    report_bugs = {
+        item["pkg"]: (item["proposed_version"], item["bugs"])
+        for item in report.get(release.name) or []}
+
+    logger.debug("listing %s-proposed sources", release.name)
+    release_sources = proposed_sources(archive, release)
+    logger.debug("listing %s-proposed sources", devel.name)
+    devel_sources = proposed_sources(archive, devel)
+
+    candidates = [
+        (name, version, spph)
+        for name in sorted(release_sources)
+        for version, spph in sorted(release_sources[name].items())
+        if version in devel_sources.get(name, {})]
+    logger.info(
+        "%d package(s) in both %s-proposed and %s-proposed",
+        len(candidates), release.name, devel.name)
+    if args.limit is not None and len(candidates) > args.limit:
+        logger.info("limiting to the first %d", args.limit)
+        del candidates[args.limit:]
+
+    removals = []
+    failures = 0
+    checked = 0
+    completed = False
+    try:
+        for name, version, spph in candidates:
+            checked += 1
+            logger.debug(
+                "[%d/%d] checking %s %s",
+                checked, len(candidates), name, version)
+            removable = check_candidate(
+                archive, release, name, version, spph, report_bugs,
+                set(args.ignored_bugs))
+            if removable is None:
+                failures += 1
+            elif removable:
+                removals.append((name, version))
+        completed = True
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        pass
+    finally:
+        # Also reached on unexpected errors, so that work done so far is
+        # not lost.
+        if not completed:
+            logger.warning(
+                "aborted while checking candidate %d/%d; "
+                "printing partial results", checked, len(candidates))
+        print_commands("%s-proposed" % release.name, reason, removals)
+    if not completed:
+        return 130
+    if failures:
+        logger.error("%d package(s) skipped due to network errors", failures)
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    try:
+        sys.exit(main())
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        logger.warning("aborted before any candidate was checked")
+        sys.exit(130)
